title: Notification abstraction with channel failover
description: One interface over WhatsApp, Slack and email with ordered failover, so an alert that matters always lands somewhere.
acceptance: A single interface covers all channels; adding a channel does not change calling code
Failover order is configurable per tenant and defaults to WhatsApp, Slack, email, dashboard banner
Delivery is retried with backoff and every attempt is recorded
Delivery status is queryable per alert
An alert that fails on every channel raises an operational page

tests.desc: Primary channel failure falls through to the secondary
All channels failing raises an operational page
Delivery attempts are recorded with their outcome
Duplicate suppression prevents the same alert being sent twice on one channel

title: WhatsApp Cloud API integration with interactive approval
description: The channel the brief's owner actually reads at 2am, with an Approve button and a Call Me First option.
acceptance: Approved message templates cover critical, high and digest alert types
Interactive buttons map to approval and escalation actions
Inbound webhooks are signature-verified before processing
Opt-in and opt-out are handled per regulation and recorded
Template rejection by Meta is surfaced to operations, not silently retried

tests.desc: A critical alert is delivered against the sandbox with buttons rendered
A webhook with an invalid signature is rejected
Button tap resolves to the correct case and action
Opt-out stops delivery and is recorded

title: Signed single-use approval tokens
description: Implements the token half of ADR-0007. Bound to one action on one case for one tenant, 15-minute expiry, single use, GET never mutates.
acceptance: Token payload binds case_id, action_id, tenant_id, approver_id, nonce and expiry, HMAC-signed
Expiry is 15 minutes and is enforced server-side
The nonce is burned on first use in Redis with a Postgres fallback
GET renders a confirmation page only; execution requires POST
Invalid, expired, reused or malformed tokens fail closed and are audited

tests.desc: A replayed token is rejected on second use
An expired token is rejected
A tampered payload fails signature verification
A token for case A cannot approve an action on case B
A GET from a link-preview user agent executes nothing
Redis unavailability falls back to the Postgres uniqueness constraint and still enforces single use

title: Step-up authentication for destructive actions
description: A valid token is necessary but not sufficient for the actions that hurt most. disable_user, isolate_device and force_password_reset require re-authentication regardless.
acceptance: Playbooks declare whether they require step-up authentication
Step-up is enforced server-side at execution, not at the UI
The step-up challenge is usable from a phone in under 30 seconds
Step-up completion is recorded in the audit entry for the action
A failed step-up leaves the case in awaiting_approval

tests.desc: A destructive action with a valid token but no step-up is refused
Bypassing the UI and calling the API directly still requires step-up
Successful step-up is recorded in the audit entry
Failed step-up returns the case to awaiting_approval

title: Response playbook registry and executor
description: Idempotent playbooks with declared blast radius and documented reversal: disable_user, revoke_sessions, delete_inbox_rule, block_ip, force_password_reset, isolate_device.
acceptance: Each playbook declares blast radius, required scopes, step-up requirement and reversal procedure
Execution is idempotent — repeating it produces the same end state without a second side effect
Pre-execution validation confirms the target still matches the case's premise
Partial failure leaves a recorded, recoverable state with explicit manual steps
Every execution writes an audit entry before and after

tests.desc: Each playbook executes correctly against a Microsoft test tenant
Repeated execution is idempotent
A playbook whose target no longer matches the premise refuses to execute
Partial failure returns the case to awaiting_approval with manual steps shown
Every registered playbook declares a reversal procedure

title: Pre-approved action policy
description: The brief's 'customers can later allow specific safe actions to run automatically — their choice, their control.' Opt-in, scoped, revocable and fully audited.
acceptance: Pre-approval is opt-in per playbook, never on by default
Destructive playbooks cannot be pre-approved at all
Pre-approval is revocable immediately and takes effect on the next action
Granting, using and revoking pre-approval are all audited
Automatically executed actions are reported to the tenant within the hour

tests.desc: A pre-approved action executes without a prompt and is audited
A destructive playbook cannot be pre-approved
Revocation takes effect on the next action
An automatic execution notifies the tenant within the window

title: Slack app with interactive approval
description: The channel MSPs and startups live in, with the same approval semantics as WhatsApp.
acceptance: OAuth installation flow per tenant workspace
Interactive blocks render the alert with Approve and Call Me First
Request signatures are verified and timestamps checked against replay
Channel routing is configurable per severity
Uninstalling the app cleanly disables the channel and fails over

tests.desc: Installation flow completes and posts a test alert
An invalid request signature is rejected
A replayed interaction payload is rejected on timestamp
Uninstall disables the channel and triggers failover

title: Email alerting and transactional delivery
description: The universal fallback channel, with deliverability configured properly so security alerts do not land in spam.
acceptance: SPF, DKIM and DMARC are configured and verified
Templates render correctly in major clients including Outlook
Approval links carry the same token semantics as other channels
Bounces and complaints are processed and surfaced
Plain-text alternative is always included

tests.desc: Delivery succeeds with passing authentication checks
Template renders without breakage across the client matrix
A bounce is processed and surfaced on the tenant's channel health

title: Action audit integration and tamper-evidence verification
description: Every alert, approval, execution and failure enters the hash-chained log, with the chain verified continuously.
acceptance: Alert sent, approval granted, action started, action completed and action failed are all audited
Audit entries distinguish AI-initiated from human-approved
Audit writes share a transaction with the state change they describe
Chain verification runs on a schedule and alerts on any break
An audit export for a tenant and date range is available for compliance

tests.desc: A full alert-to-action flow produces the complete expected audit sequence
A failed action still produces a complete audit record
Chain verification detects an induced break
Audit export contains every entry for the requested range and nothing outside it

title: End-to-end BEC scenario test
description: The P5 exit criterion: reproduce the brief's scenario as an automated test — 02:14 impossible travel, 02:17 inbox rule, 02:18 alert, 02:21 fixed.
acceptance: Seeds the exact event sequence from the brief
Asserts one case, not three separate alerts
Asserts the alert is delivered within 3 minutes of the second signal
Asserts approval executes both remediation actions
Asserts the complete audit chain verifies afterwards

tests.desc: Full scenario completes within the latency budget
Exactly one case is produced from the two signals
Approval executes both revoke_sessions and delete_inbox_rule
Audit chain verifies across the whole scenario

title: Response runbooks and failure procedures
description: What an operator does when an action fails, a token secret must be rotated, or a playbook causes customer impact.
acceptance: A runbook exists for each documented failure mode in the architecture failure table
Approval token secret rotation is documented with overlapping validity
Each playbook's reversal procedure is written and verified by execution
Customer communication templates exist for an action that caused impact

tests.desc: An operator executes each reversal procedure successfully in a test tenant
Token secret rotation is performed with no failed approvals during the overlap
